selection: mpg123 has the highest Homebrew install-on-request count (12,256) among hits whose own C library decodes MPEG Layer III frames from a documented byte API. lame (6,992) ranks next but its HIP decoder is built over libmpg123. mad (libmad 0.16.5, 1,145) is the next independent decoder family and is verified through mad_stream_buffer/mad_frame_decode/mad_synth_frame.
uncertainty: Two verified paths from two independent decoder families; no lower-ranked filler entries. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad needs MAD_BUFFER_GUARD (8) zero bytes appended after the input; the harness adds exactly that and counts every recoverable error except the one LOSTSYNC at the guard. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for whole distributions (the mpg123 player and library; the mad formula library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c, and libmad is the decoder behind the SoX path there. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.
